content.content:
#### Spotlight

While a step shows, the window is dimmed, as an inset panel dims it, but for a cut-out around the part the step points at, with 4 pixels of room and corners rounded 6 pixels, outlined in the theme's accent, so that part reads as lit. The cut-out is taken from where the part is actually laid out in the window, in the window's own coordinates, each frame, so it sits exactly around it, the same 4 pixels on every side, never offset by the title bar, the ribbon, the display's scale, or a scrolled container, and never lags a frame behind it. The cut-out moves to each step's part, easing between them over 200 milliseconds, and follows it as it moves, as when the window is resized or the ribbon collapses.
Each part is the element itself, as drawn, measured as it is painted in that frame: a ribbon tab is its label with its 8 pixels either side, the full 32 pixels of the tab row tall, as the ribbon draws it, and a chat input tab the same in the chat input's tab bar, Chain the width of its icon's tab; the chat input's tabs, together, run from the left edge of Code to the right edge of Freeform, the help text beside them left out. Never a parent, a row, a group, or the whole bar holding it, and never a size guessed or kept from an earlier frame. Where the 4 pixels of room would go past the window's edge, as above a ribbon tab at the top of the window, the cut-out stops at the edge on that side, still exactly 4 pixels from the part on every other side. The accent outline, 2 pixels wide, is drawn just outside the cut-out's edge, following its rounded corners, from the same rectangle, so the ring and the cut-out never part. A step whose part hasn't been painted yet, as a tab that has only just been selected, shows nothing until it has, rather than a cut-out or callout placed anywhere else.
Beside it sits the callout, a card on the theme's raised surface with corners rounded 8 pixels, a border, and a shadow, 320 pixels wide, or the window's width less 32 pixels where that is narrower, as tall as what it holds. It is placed beneath the cut-out, 12 pixels from it, where it fits there, and otherwise above it, to its right, or to its left, in that order, the first side it fits on whole. Beneath or above, it is centred on the cut-out horizontally; to a side, it is centred on it vertically. Where centring would put it closer than 16 pixels to the window's edge, it is slid along that edge until it is 16 pixels in, and never off the window, nor over the cut-out. Fitting on a side means fitting whole between the cut-out, with its 12 pixels, and the window's edge less 16 pixels, so for a part near the window's bottom, as the chat input's tabs, the callout goes above it, its pointer beneath it pointing down at the part, never beneath it, covering it. Where it fits on no side whole, it goes on the side with the most room, as tall as that room, its text scrolling, and still never over the cut-out. Its pointer, a triangle 12 pixels wide and 6 deep in the card's colour, with its border, sits on the card's edge facing the cut-out, pointing at the cut-out's centre wherever the card was slid, but never nearer than 12 pixels to the card's corners. When the part moves, the callout moves with the cut-out, easing with it.
It holds, with 16 pixels of padding, left aligned: the step's title, in the body's text colour, semibold, then 8 pixels beneath it its text as a paragraph or two, wrapping within the card, then 12 pixels beneath that a footer row. In the footer, "Skip tour", a muted link, sits at the left, and "Step N of M", muted, and then a Back button, disabled on the first step, and a primary Next button, reading "Done" on the last step, 8 pixels apart, sit at the right, everything in the row centred on one line vertically. It is drawn in the theme's roles, in dark mode and light.
While a step shows, only the callout and the part lit take the mouse, and clicks on the dimmed window do nothing, so the walkthrough is never left by accident. <Escape> skips the tour, as Skip tour does, and <Enter>, while Next is enabled, goes to the next step.

#### Steps

content.text:
Both are fixed: the tour's callout now sits above the mode tabs and points down at them, and the Project tab's ring fits the tab. All 500 tests pass with no warnings, and a Windows type-check is clean. I've only checked this in tests, not in the running app.

**The callout on the mode tabs:** "the chat input's tabs" was measuring the whole tab bar, including the help text and buttons along it (1660 px wide in the test window). The highlight covered all of that, and the callout centred far from the actual tabs. That step now lights only Code through Freeform. The test confirms the callout sits 12 px above the highlight, centred on the tabs, with its pointer aimed down at them.

**The Project tab's ring:**
- **At the top edge:** the tab touches the top of the window, so the 4 px of room above it went off-screen and the ring's top edge was lost. The highlight now stops at the window's edge and keeps exactly 4 px on the other three sides.
- **Ring placement:** the ring was drawn inside the highlight's edge. It's now drawn just outside it, 2 px wide, from the same rectangle and following the rounded corners, so the two can't drift apart.
